data.title: Anthropic confirms $83 IPO price on 980 million shares in an $81 billion deal
data.description:
The size of the deal is the main market story. Absorbing roughly $81 billion of new stock, and potentially more if the over-allotment option is used, draws liquidity from elsewhere. That could weigh on other AI and mega-cap tech names in the short term as funds rebalance to make room. A strong debut would likely help neocloud and AI infrastructure stocks, which sold off this week on funding worries, while a weak one would reinforce them. The over-allotment option also gives underwriters a tool to support the price in the early days of trading, which may soften any initial volatility.

---

data.title: Moody’s keeps US rating at Aa1 as the economy beats forecasts, seeing 2.3% growth this year
data.description:
A stable Aa1 outlook removes one source of headline risk for Treasuries, but the growth upgrade cuts the other way for bonds. Stronger-than-expected activity strengthens the hawkish case being made by Fed officials this week and supports pricing for a December hike, which should keep front-end yields and the dollar firm. That’s a headwind for gold, which has tended to fall as Fed hike expectations build. Moody’s flagged energy prices as a drag on growth, a reminder that oil is the swing factor: further strength in crude would hurt growth and keep inflation pressure alive at the same time.

--

data.title: UBS says the AI sell-off is a reset, not a collapse, and backs eurozone stocks and bonds
data.description: The UBS view gives some support to dip-buyers, but how much it helps depends on the breadth test it sets. As long as selling stays concentrated in chips, neoclouds and richly valued growth names, the bank’s case holds. A spread into banks and industrials would challenge it. Rates are the main threat. With four Fed officials sounding hawkish on Wednesday alone and Treasury yields already elevated, financing pressure on leveraged AI infrastructure is likely to stay in focus. The tilt toward Europe and short-dated quality bonds suggests investors may rotate within markets rather than exit them. Anthropic’s Nasdaq debut today is an early real-time read on whether risk appetite for AI is holding up.

data.title: Moody’s cuts Nvidia outlook to stable, saying Huang’s exit clouds strategy and policy
data.description:
On its own, an outlook change rarely moves equity prices, and Nvidia’s balance sheet remains among the strongest in corporate credit. The bigger signal is for bond and CDS investors: protection costs had already climbed as the leadership crisis unfolded, and Moody’s move confirms that governance risk is now being priced into Nvidia’s credit. For the wider AI trade, it is another headwind in a week already focused on Anthropic’s Nasdaq debut and Fed rate risk. Asian suppliers such as TSMC and the memory makers could be sensitive to any sign that Nvidia’s partners are rethinking their ties to the company.

---

data.title: BOJ tipped to hike to 1.50% in December, its first three-hike year in 37 years
data.description:
With a December hike now the clear consensus, the bigger surprise for the yen would be a hold. That would likely send USD/JPY back toward the levels that prompted heavy intervention. A hike on its own may do little to lift the yen while the Fed is also tightening, so traders are likely to focus on whether Ueda signals the faster path to 1.75% that the poll now expects. Front-end JGB yields have room to rise further if that guidance comes through. The Nikkei faces a double headwind from higher domestic rates and the shaky AI trade, which leaves exporters relying more heavily on a weak yen for support.

---
Japan’s economy is shrinking and its stock market is sliding, but with inflation above target and the yen near 160, economists expect the BOJ to keep hiking, first in December and again by March.

data.title: Anthropic prices IPO at $83, above range, setting up Thursday’s Nasdaq debut as ANT
data.description:
How ANT trades on debut is likely to shape sentiment across the wider AI complex. Nvidia, AMD, Microsoft, Amazon and Google are all investors, partners or suppliers, so their shares may react to how ANT opens. Asian chip and memory stocks that supply AI hardware could feel the knock-on effect in Friday’s session. Rates are the main risk to the AI trade. With several Fed officials leaning toward further hikes, any rise in Treasury yields would sharpen worries about funding costs for data centres and neoclouds. A strong debut could ease those worries for now, while a soft one would add to them.

---

data.title: Kashkari says markets see more Fed hikes than officials do as four Fed voices turn hawkish
data.description:
Hawkish Fed remarks arriving one after another should support the US dollar and keep front-end Treasury yields firm going into December. Gold is the asset most exposed. Through this cycle it has fallen as Fed hike expectations build, so more tightening talk is a headwind rather than a bid. For the Australian dollar, which is already near 10-month lows, a Fed that keeps hiking narrows the policy gap with the RBA. That raises the stakes for today’s Australian jobs data. If Kashkari is right that the shocks behind inflation are supply-driven, oil remains the key input to watch, because further energy price spikes would strengthen the hawks’ case.

data.title: NZDUSD sellers stay in control as price nears the 0.54808 floor
data.description:
The NZDUSD decline started on November 10 after the pair tested the upper channel trend line and turned lower, breaking below both its 200-hour and 100-hour moving averages. The go-ahead for more downside came the next day when the price bounced back to the 200-hour moving average and sellers leaned against it. That rejection set up six days of selling that took the pair to a low of 0.54808 yesterday.

Since then, the price has been consolidating. Yesterday’s bounce stalled at 0.55057, and today’s high reached nearly the same level at 0.5506. Today’s low came in at 0.5484, just above yesterday’s low. With the pair trading near 0.5488, the price is still closer to the floor of the range than the ceiling.

data.title: The market's verdict on Nvidia earnings is a problem for the AI boom trade
data.description:
With each passing day, the probability is rising that the AI boom is coming to an end.

Nvidia reported good earnings yesterday and the guidance was upbeat. At the very least, there was no sign of trouble in the earnings numbers. Shares initially cheered, rising more than 5% after hours but that disappeared at the open and NVDA is now down 2.3% on the day.

data.title: BoC’s Gravelle says policy scenarios help build credibility
data.description:
Bank of Canada Deputy Governor Toni Gravelle discussed how the central bank uses scenarios to explain how it might respond as economic conditions change.

  • Bank of Canada scenarios are designed to help keep the BoC accountable and build credibility.
  • When the public trusts the BoC to keep inflation around 2%, their inflation expectations stay anchored.
  • If inflation expectations are anchored, that makes monetary policy more effective.
  • By helping market participants understand how we tend to react when conditions change, we can shape their expectations.
  • Bank of Canada says scenarios help make monetary policy more effective.
  • If businesses expect the BoC will get inflation back down to 2%, they are less likely to build higher inflation into their prices.
  • That decision helps keep inflation in check and reduces barriers to getting it back to target.

data.title: Fed’s Daly says inflation has been too high for too long as consumer spending holds up
data.description:
Comments from the Fed’s Daly on inflation, consumer spending and employment crossed the wires.

  • Employment is broad-based and seeing manufacturing resurgence.
  • Consumer spending is resilient, even at the bottom of the income level. Inflation has been too high for too long.
